extracted.intended_audience: mathematicians and authors of mathematical papers, notes, monographs, and books preparing manuscripts for publication
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for composing clear, effective mathematical writing: organization, presentation of results, mathematical English and notation, revision, and manuscript mechanics for submission and publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Value of good mathematical writing
rubrics_metrics.description: Good writing conveys more than the author originally had in mind; poor writing conveys less. Well written papers are more quickly accepted, printed, read and appreciated; for notes, monographs, and books writing quality is especially important.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasizes that clear, forceful writing increases acceptance and readership; motivates investing effort in style and clarity. The manual aims to alert authors to opportunities for better writing through precept and example.

rubrics_metrics.name: Introduction (section 1)
rubrics_metrics.description: General opening guidance for the manual and for beginning a piece of mathematical writing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sets context for principles that follow; introduces why structure, clarity, and style matter. (Page lists as primary section; detailed guidance is in the book itself.)

rubrics_metrics.name: General Organization (section 2)
rubrics_metrics.description: Overall organization of a mathematical paper or manuscript.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers high-level structural choices that affect readability and flow; includes title, introduction, prerequisites, notation, organization and pacing. Good organization helps readers understand the results and proofs.

rubrics_metrics.name: The title (2.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: Choosing an effective title for a mathematical paper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Title should accurately reflect the paper's content and attract the right readers; be concise and informative. (Listed as a discrete topic in the table of contents.)

rubrics_metrics.name: The introduction (2.2)
rubrics_metrics.description: How to write the introduction to a paper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Introduction should orient the reader: state the problem, summarize main results and context, and indicate structure of the paper. Aim for clarity and appropriate level of background.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prerequisites (2.3)
rubrics_metrics.description: Determining and stating what background the reader needs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State assumed knowledge explicitly to set reader expectations; avoid unnecessary prerequisites; indicate references for background material.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notation and terminology (2.4)
rubrics_metrics.description: Choosing and presenting notation and terms used in the paper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Introduce notation clearly and consistently; prefer simple, standard notation when possible; avoid overloading symbols and explain nonstandard terms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Organization and pace (2.5)
rubrics_metrics.description: Structuring material and controlling the pacing through the paper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Arrange results, examples, and proofs so the reader is neither overwhelmed nor bored; balance exposition and technical detail; guide readers through complex arguments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presenting Your Results (section 3)
rubrics_metrics.description: Principles for stating and organizing mathematical results before proving them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasizes how to present theorems, propositions, and their proofs for maximal clarity; includes concrete rules like stating results before proofs and managing generality and style.

rubrics_metrics.name: State first, prove second (3.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: State a result (theorem/lemma) before presenting its proof.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Readers should see the statement and understand its significance before diving into technical proofs. Keeps exposition reader-centered and helps comprehension.

rubrics_metrics.name: Generality (3.2)
rubrics_metrics.description: Choosing the appropriate level of generality for results and statements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid excessive generality that obscures ideas; present results at a level that clarifies the concept and makes proofs intelligible. Balance general statements with motivating special cases or examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Style (3.3)
rubrics_metrics.description: Mathematical expository style when presenting results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aim for clarity, concision, and readability; choose wording and structure that communicate ideas rather than merely record them. Use examples and intuition where helpful.

rubrics_metrics.name: The character of a proof (3.4)
rubrics_metrics.description: How proofs should be written to serve the reader.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proofs should show the argument's structure, highlight key ideas, and avoid unnecessary detours. Make the 'why' and 'how' clear; give roadmaps for long proofs and separate technical lemmas when appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Keeping the reader informed (3.5)
rubrics_metrics.description: Techniques to keep readers oriented through exposition and proofs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use signposting, summaries, and reminders of notation and hypotheses; state what will be proved and why steps are taken. Prevent reader confusion by indicating strategy and progress.

rubrics_metrics.name: Citing reasons (3.6)
rubrics_metrics.description: Explicitly indicate reasons or justifications used in arguments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When a step uses a lemma, theorem, or standard fact, cite it clearly so the reader can verify or recall it. Don't leave justifications implicit when they are nonobvious.

rubrics_metrics.name: Citing references (3.7)
rubrics_metrics.description: How to reference prior work and literature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Give precise citations for results used or compared; distinguish between background sources and directly used references. Cite responsibly and consistently to help readers follow context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proofs by contradiction (3.8)
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidelines for using indirect proof techniques.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use proofs by contradiction when natural; however, prefer direct proofs when they illuminate the mechanism. Make the structure of a contradiction proof explicit and avoid obscure negations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mathematical English (section 4)
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules and guidance on the use of English in mathematical writing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers voice (we/I), grammar of mixing symbols and words, conditional constructions, and precision in definitions. Aims to make mathematical English clear and conventional.

rubrics_metrics.name: We and I (4.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance on first-person usage in mathematical writing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discusses when to use 'we' vs 'I' for the authorial voice; conventions vary by context, but choose a consistent, reader-friendly voice (often 'we' for mathematical exposition).

rubrics_metrics.name: The grammar of symbols (4.2)
rubrics_metrics.description: How symbols should interact with sentence grammar.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat formulas as grammatical objects within sentences; ensure punctuation and sentence structure remain correct when symbols are embedded. Avoid fragmentary sentences formed by math notation.

rubrics_metrics.name: If . . . , then . . . (4.3)
rubrics_metrics.description: Proper presentation of conditional statements and logical structure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Write conditional claims clearly; align informal 'if...then' phrasing with formal logical structure to avoid ambiguity. State hypotheses explicitly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definitions (4.4)
rubrics_metrics.description: How to craft and present mathematical definitions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Give clear, concise definitions; motivate them and provide examples. Avoid circularity and unnecessary complexity; specify scope and notation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Symbols (section 5)
rubrics_metrics.description: Principles for choosing and using mathematical symbols.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advice on limiting symbol proliferation, choosing notation, typographical appearance, integrating symbols with text, numbering, indices, and suppressing redundant information.

rubrics_metrics.name: You can do with fewer than you think (5.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: Advice to limit the number of distinct symbols used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Excessive symbols burden readers; reuse understandable notation and minimize new symbols to what is necessary for clarity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Choice of notation (5.2)
rubrics_metrics.description: Choosing notation that is clear and conventional.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer standard, mnemonic notation; avoid choices that conflict with established conventions in the subject or that obscure meaning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Look (5.3)
rubrics_metrics.description: Visual appearance of mathematical notation and displays.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider legibility, font choices, spacing, and alignment to improve readability; good 'look' reduces reader effort.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mixing symbols with text (5.4)
rubrics_metrics.description: How to integrate mathematical symbols into running text.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure sentences remain grammatical when symbols are embedded; provide surrounding words that make the logical flow clear.

rubrics_metrics.name: Your numbering system (5.5)
rubrics_metrics.description: Numbering theorems, equations, sections, figures, etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use a consistent, logical numbering scheme that helps cross-referencing and navigation; avoid confusing or redundant numbering.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multiple indices (5.6)
rubrics_metrics.description: Handling objects with multiple subscripts/superscripts or indices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid cumbersome multiple indices when possible; introduce notation to manage complexity and keep expressions readable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suppress useless information (5.7)
rubrics_metrics.description: Remove notation or details that don't aid understanding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Eliminate redundant qualifiers, unnecessary symbols, or clutter that distracts from key ideas.

rubrics_metrics.name: English Usage (section 6)
rubrics_metrics.description: Practical matters of prose, word choice, grammar, spelling, punctuation, and idioms in mathematical English.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Improve prose clarity by attending to common usage issues and distinctions in meaning; maintain professional and conventional language.

rubrics_metrics.name: Style (6.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: General stylistic advice for mathematical English.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Favor clarity, brevity, and directness; choose sentence structure and vocabulary suitable for the intended audience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Some distinctions in meaning (6.2)
rubrics_metrics.description: Clarify words or phrases that are easily confused in mathematical contexts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be precise with terminology; prefer words whose mathematical meaning matches the intended sense; explain potentially ambiguous terms.

rubrics_metrics.name: A few matters of grammar (6.3)
rubrics_metrics.description: Specific grammar points relevant to mathematical writing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Attend to subject-verb agreement, pronoun reference, and other grammatical details that affect clarity of exposition.

rubrics_metrics.name: In terms of (6.4)
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage considerations for the phrase 'in terms of' and similar constructions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use such constructions carefully to avoid awkward or unclear phrasing; prefer simpler alternatives when possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Some distinctions in spelling (6.5)
rubrics_metrics.description: Spelling variants and conventions (e.g., British vs American) relevant to mathematical writing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be consistent in spelling across a manuscript; follow the journal or publisher's conventions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Some ups and downs of punctuation (6.6)
rubrics_metrics.description: Punctuation rules and conventions in mathematical prose.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use punctuation to clarify sentence structure, especially around displayed equations and embedded clauses; avoid punctuation that breaks mathematical readability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Latin words (6.7)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of Latin phrases (e.g., 'et al.', 'i.e.', 'e.g.') in mathematical writing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use Latin terms sparingly and correctly; prefer plain English when it improves clarity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-plan ahead for the future in advance (6.8)
rubrics_metrics.description: Cautionary note about tautological or redundant phrases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid redundant collocations and clichés that clutter prose (the section title is itself an example of redundancy).

rubrics_metrics.name: Revise, Revise (section 7)
rubrics_metrics.description: Emphasis on revision as a critical step in writing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Iterative revision improves clarity, correctness, and style; authors should edit for organization, exposition, notation, and mechanical errors before submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mechanics (section 8)
rubrics_metrics.description: Practical mechanical aspects of preparing a manuscript for submission and publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers preparing a clean manuscript, spacing, displays, figures/tables, conforming to journal conventions, marking manuscripts and galleys, proofreading, and the submission process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submit a clean manuscript (8.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: Prepare a tidy, well-formatted manuscript for submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow journal guidelines, ensure readable typesetting, and eliminate avoidable errors; provide necessary files and clear organization for editors and referees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Spacing (8.2)
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidelines on line spacing, paragraph spacing, and white space.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use spacing to improve readability of text and displays; follow publisher or journal specifications for manuscript formatting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Displays (8.3)
rubrics_metrics.description: Formatting and presenting displayed equations and mathematical displays.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Arrange displays for readability, align equations logically, number only as needed, and integrate displays into the narrative to maintain flow.

rubrics_metrics.name: Figures and tables (8.4)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use and formatting of figures and tables in mathematical work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include clear captions, label axes and elements, ensure figures add value, and follow journal specifications for figure files and resolution.

rubrics_metrics.name: The conventions of the journal (8.5)
rubrics_metrics.description: Adhere to the stylistic and mechanical conventions of the target journal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check and follow submission instructions, citation format, notation preferences, and other publisher rules to avoid delays or rework.

rubrics_metrics.name: Marking the manuscript (8.6)
rubrics_metrics.description: How to annotate or mark manuscripts for editors, typesetters, and coauthors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use clear, unambiguous markup for corrections and comments; follow journal instructions for marked-up manuscripts to facilitate production.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proofreading your manuscript (8.7)
rubrics_metrics.description: Careful checking of text, mathematics, and formatting before submission and at proof stage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proofread for mathematical correctness, typographical errors, consistent notation, and clarity; solicit colleagues for critical reading when possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: The odyssey of a manuscript (8.8)
rubrics_metrics.description: The process and stages a manuscript goes through from submission to publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prepare for review, revision, resubmission, and production stages; understand timelines and editorial workflows to manage expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Marking the galleys (8.9)
rubrics_metrics.description: How to review and mark publisher galleys (proofs) before final publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check galleys carefully for production errors, mis-set mathematics, and typographical issues; respond promptly and clearly to proof queries.

rubrics_metrics.name: APPENDIX: The Use of Symbols: A Case Study
rubrics_metrics.description: A focused case study illustrating principles for symbol use.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical examples that demonstrate the book's advice on notation choice, clarity, and suppression of unnecessary complexity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Annotated Bibliography
rubrics_metrics.description: References and suggested further reading on mathematical writing and style.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides sources for deeper study and examples; useful for authors seeking more detailed guidance or alternative viewpoints.
